fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker calls GET /rest/memories, which server.ts:630 registers without authentication. getMemories() runs MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) at routes/memory.ts:24 without an attributes restriction, returning every memory together with its owner's user record.

shortDescription.text: An anonymous attacker browses /support/logs, which server.ts:281 serves with serveIndex over the logs directory and server.ts:283 serves file contents without authentication.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker uploads an .xml file to POST /file-upload declaring an external entity that references a local file. handleXmlUpload() passes the content to parseXmlString(), which enables XML_PARSE_NOENT and XML_PARSE_DTDLOAD at lib/xml.ts:35 with host filesystem input providers registered, and the expanded document is echoed back in the 410 error message (routes/fileUpload.ts:79).

fullDescription.text: An authenticated user POSTs /profile/image/url with imageUrl pointing at an internal service or cloud metadata address. profileImageUrlUpload() calls fetch(url) at routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24 with no scheme or host allow-list and writes the response body to a publicly served file under assets/public/images/uploads/<id>.jpg, so the attacker downloads the internal response.

fullDescription.text: An attacker brute-forcing security answers rotates a forged X-Forwarded-For header on each request to /rest/user/reset-password. app.enable('trust proxy') at server.ts:342 makes req.ip the attacker-supplied left-most header value, and the rateLimit keyGenerator at server.ts:346 falls back to that ip, so every request gets a fresh rate-limit bucket.

fullDescription.text: An attacker sends victims a link to /redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. isRedirectAllowed() accepts any URL that merely contains an allow-listed entry (url.includes at lib/insecurity.ts:136), and performRedirect() redirects the browser to the attacker host under the shop's domain.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker opens a raw Socket.IO client to the shop's HTTP listener; the connection handler accepts it without any token or session check, so the attacker acts as a legitimate player client, receives every challenge-solved notification and can emit the verify* and notification events that mutate server-side challenge state.

fullDescription.text: An attacker z85-encodes the string '<current MMMYY>-99' and applies it via PUT /rest/basket/:id/coupon/:coupon. generateCoupon() at lib/insecurity.ts:99 produces coupons by plain encoding with no secret, and discountFromCoupon() trusts any value whose decoded month matches.

shortDescription.text: An attacker hosts a page that auto-submits a form POST to /profile.

fullDescription.text: An attacker hosts a page that auto-submits a form POST to /profile. updateUserProfile() authenticates solely by the token cookie at routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17, the cookie is set without SameSite at lib/insecurity.ts:192, and no CSRF token is checked, so a logged-in victim's username is changed by the attacker's page.

fullDescription.text: LLM01 Prompt Injection / LLM05 / LLM06: an anonymous user crafts chat messages that persuade the model to call generateCoupon with a large discount. The tool schema at routes/chat.ts:179 accepts any number, and execute() issues a valid coupon via security.generateCoupon at routes/chat.ts:184; the 10% cap and eligibility rules exist only as system-prompt text.

fullDescription.text: LLM07 System Prompt Leakage: an anonymous user asks the chatbot to repeat its instructions. buildSystemPrompt() embeds a confidential 15% courtesy-discount escalation rule at routes/chat.ts:105, and the model can disclose it because nothing outside the prompt protects it.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker repeatedly uploads small YAML alias-expansion or XML entity-expansion documents to POST /file-upload. handleYamlUpload() runs yaml.load inside vm.runInContext with a 2000 ms timeout at routes/fileUpload.ts:109 (and parseXmlString does the same at lib/xml.ts:38); the synchronous parse occupies the single Node.js event loop for up to two seconds per request.

shortDescription.text: The open question 'Does the process require separation between requester and approver?' cannot be resolved from code alone.

fullDescription.text: The open question 'Does the process require separation between requester and approver?' cannot be resolved from code alone. The product review system has no formal approval workflow: liking a review (routes/likeProductReviews.ts:31) only prevents double-liking but not self-liking, and any authenticated user can edit any review (routes/updateProductReviews.ts:17-20) without ownership enforcement. Whether 'liking' constitutes a required approval gate is a business policy determination the code does not encode.

shortDescription.text: Role checks (isAccounting, isDeluxe, isCustomer) and the authenticatedUsers.tokenMap read exclusively from the JWT token payload, never from the database.

fullDescription.text: Role checks (isAccounting, isDeluxe, isCustomer) and the authenticatedUsers.tokenMap read exclusively from the JWT token payload, never from the database. No token revocation list or blacklist exists. If an admin changes a user's role in the database, or soft-deletes an account (deletedAt), the user's existing JWT (valid 6 hours) retains the old role and all associated access. The 6-hour lifetime is hardcoded with no documented policy accepting it as an explicit revocation delay, so the exclusion does not apply.

shortDescription.text: The server registers a 'verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge' WebSocket event that checks only Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 1; any unauthenticated socket can emit this event with a trivial payload (e.g.

fullDescription.text: The server registers a 'verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge' WebSocket event that checks only Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 1; any unauthenticated socket can emit this event with a trivial payload (e.g. [1,2]) to trigger challengeUtils.solveIf and mark the challenge solved. No authentication or session check is applied to any WebSocket event handler. The exclusion (server-side verification of challenge state) is absent: the server validates only payload shape, not whether the user actually dismissed multiple notifications. Other verify events (verifyLocalXssChallenge, verifySvgInjectionChallenge) require knowledge of specific payloads and are harder to abuse; the closeNotifications case has no such protection.

shortDescription.text: The memories query in the data export uses req.body.UserId (attacker-controlled) instead of the authenticated user's own id (loggedInUser.data.id).

fullDescription.text: The memories query in the data export uses req.body.UserId (attacker-controlled) instead of the authenticated user's own id (loggedInUser.data.id). An authenticated user can retrieve another user's memories by supplying a different UserId in the request body. Orders and reviews are scoped to the authenticated user's email, but the memories portion of the export is unscoped.

message.text: An anonymous attacker repeatedly uploads small YAML alias-expansion or XML entity-expansion documents to POST /file-upload. handleYamlUpload() runs yaml.load inside vm.runInContext with a 2000 ms timeout at routes/fileUpload.ts:109 (and parseXmlString does the same at lib/xml.ts:38); the synchronous parse occupies the single Node.js event loop for up to two seconds per request.

description.text: Bound parser and decompression resource limits

message.text: LLM10 Unbounded Consumption: an anonymous client floods POST /rest/chat (no auth or rate limit, server.ts:638) with long message histories. chat() forwards the client-supplied messages array to streamText at routes/chat.ts:203 with up to 10 tool steps and no maxOutputTokens, message-count or size limit, so each request consumes provider tokens and server connections.

description.text: Cap tokens, history and request rate

message.text: An unauthenticated attacker scripts many POSTs to /rest/web3/walletExploitAddress, each with a large unique walletAddress string; every value is added to the process-wide walletsConnected Set and is only removed when a matching on-chain ContractExploited event arrives, so heap usage grows until the Node process slows or crashes.

description.text: Validate and bound walletsConnected

message.text: When the Alchemy RPC socket errors (for example ALCHEMY_API_KEY is unset or invalid), the onerror handler resets isEventListenerCreated without destroying the provider; an anonymous attacker then repeatedly calls GET /rest/web3/nftMintListen so each call opens another WebSocketProvider and contract listener that is never closed.

description.text: Destroy failed providers and serialize listener creation in nftMint.ts and web3Wallet.ts

message.text: A low-privilege customer calls GET /rest/user/authentication-details with their own token; retrieveUserList() at line 12 returns every user's email, role, deluxeToken, lastLoginIp, and last login time because the handler performs no role check and the route is guarded only by isAuthorized().

description.text: Require admin role

message.text: An attacker who gets code running in any ci.yml job, for example through a poisoned dependency or the mutable coverallsapp/github-action@v2 reference, uses the inherited GITHUB_TOKEN; if the repository default token scope is read-write, the token can push commits, edit releases, or alter workflows.

description.text: Drop unnecessary privileges in build and runtime

message.text: Container Runs as Root: Containers running as root expand container-escape blast radius.

description.text: Add non-root USER instruction to test/smoke/Dockerfile

message.text: Missing Workflow Permissions Block: Without an explicit permissions block at workflow or job level, the job inherits the repository default (commonly write-all) for GITHUB_TOKEN — any compromised step can push code, create releases, or approve PRs.

description.text: Add least-privilege permissions blocks to all workflows lacking them

message.text: An authenticated customer POSTs /rest/deluxe-membership with paymentMode set to any value other than 'wallet' or 'card'. upgradeToDeluxe() skips both payment branches and assigns the deluxe role and token at routes/deluxe.ts:43.

description.text: Require successful payment before deluxe upgrade

message.text: Token exfiltrated from local/session storage via the Step 1 payload.

description.text: Store session tokens in HttpOnly cookies

message.text: Exfiltrated token accepted for a new session; absence of token binding / PKCE removes the last server-side revocation opportunity.

description.text: Harden the authentication flow

message.text: The open question 'Does the process require separation between requester and approver?' cannot be resolved from code alone. The product review system has no formal approval workflow: liking a review (routes/likeProductReviews.ts:31) only prevents double-liking but not self-liking, and any authenticated user can edit any review (routes/updateProductReviews.ts:17-20) without ownership enforcement. Whether 'liking' constitutes a required approval gate is a business policy determination the code does not encode.

description.text: Manual review: verify User bypasses a required approval
Enforce independent approval and invalidate approvals when the approved content changes

message.text: Role checks (isAccounting, isDeluxe, isCustomer) and the authenticatedUsers.tokenMap read exclusively from the JWT token payload, never from the database. No token revocation list or blacklist exists. If an admin changes a user's role in the database, or soft-deletes an account (deletedAt), the user's existing JWT (valid 6 hours) retains the old role and all associated access. The 6-hour lifetime is hardcoded with no documented policy accepting it as an explicit revocation delay, so the exclusion does not apply.

description.text: Re-check current roles and account status when a session or token is used

message.text: The server registers a 'verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge' WebSocket event that checks only Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 1; any unauthenticated socket can emit this event with a trivial payload (e.g. [1,2]) to trigger challengeUtils.solveIf and mark the challenge solved. No authentication or session check is applied to any WebSocket event handler. The exclusion (server-side verification of challenge state) is absent: the server validates only payload shape, not whether the user actually dismissed multiple notifications. Other verify events (verifyLocalXssChallenge, verifySvgInjectionChallenge) require knowledge of specific payloads and are harder to abuse; the closeNotifications case has no such protection.

description.text: Require authentication on every exposed endpoint (F-087)

message.text: The memories query in the data export uses req.body.UserId (attacker-controlled) instead of the authenticated user's own id (loggedInUser.data.id). An authenticated user can retrieve another user's memories by supplying a different UserId in the request body. Orders and reviews are scoped to the authenticated user's email, but the memories portion of the export is unscoped.

description.text: Enforce object-level (ownership) authorization (F-088)

message.text: placeOrder() at /rest/basket/:id/checkout takes paymentId from req.body.orderDetails.paymentId and stores it in the order record without any check that the card belongs to the authenticated user (req.body.UserId derived from JWT). An authenticated attacker can reference any card ID from any user in the checkout request body and the order will be stored referencing that card.

description.text: Enforce object-level (ownership) authorization (F-089)
